title: Verify Claude Code format assumptions on a real Mac
description:
Before writing the adapter, pin the unverifiable format assumptions against a real Mac (Ryan's): userType values distinguishing external/human from internal; promptSource values (typed vs system vs sdk); exact spellings of system-reminder, task-notification, interrupted-request, and compact-continuation markers; the queued-command attachment shape (attachment.prompt, attachment.origin.kind == human); the subagent transcript layout (subagents folders vs agent- prefixed files); whether branched/forked session copies preserve record uuids; the history-sources.json archive registry shape. Record findings in Kanbus (findings for contested observations).

Done when: every assumption is confirmed or corrected with real examples captured into synthetic fixtures; findings/comments record the evidence.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Blocked from remote verification — needs Ryan's real Mac. The adapter (KDATAP-11c4f0, KDATAP-bc0702, KDATAP-47d0f7) is implemented against the officially documented format plus community-verified shapes, with synthetic fixtures. Before or during local verification, check on the Mac and record findings here:

1. `userType` values distinguishing external/human from internal records in current Claude Code versions.
2. `promptSource` values (typed vs system vs sdk) and any new values.
3. Exact spellings of system-reminder, task-notification, interrupted-request, and compact-continuation markers in current releases.
4. The queued-command attachment shape (`attachment.prompt`, `attachment.origin.kind == human`).
5. Subagent transcript layout: `subagents` folders vs `agent-`-prefixed files under the project dir.
6. Whether branched/forked session copies preserve record uuids (dedup depends on it).
7. The history-sources.json archive registry shape.

Everything local-only; record findings as Kanbus findings if contested. Until verified, extraction tolerates unknown record types by skip-and-count.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Verified all seven assumptions against the real ~/.claude/projects corpus on this Mac (722 JSONL files, 92022 user-role records; scanned locally with a throwaway script in /tmp, counts and field names only — no message text read into any artifact).

1. userType: every user record has userType=external (92022/92022). No internal value exists in current releases; internal/injected content is distinguished by isMeta, isSidechain, promptSource, and origin fields instead.
2. promptSource: observed values typed (2), sdk (2502), system (1632), absent (87886). Genuinely typed messages mostly have promptSource absent, so the adapter's skip-only-system/sdk logic is correct; typed/sdk/system spellings confirmed.
3. Markers: <system-reminder> (307 records), <task-notification> (1884), and the compact continuation 'This session is being continued from a previous conversation' (102) confirmed verbatim. <interrupted-request> NEVER appears in the current release — interruptions surface via an interruptedByShutdown field on user records; the regex stays as defensive tolerance.
4. Queued commands: confirmed, but as standalone records, not fields on user records — type:'attachment' with attachment:{type:'queued_command', prompt, origin:{kind:'human'}, commandMode:'prompt', source_uuid, timestamp} (738 human-origin queued commands in corpus, all with non-empty string prompt and ISO timestamps). The adapter previously skipped these entirely (recall gap); it now absorbs them as human messages with queued: record ids. Other attachment types (total_tokens_reminder, environment, instructions, etc.) are injected context and stay excluded. No material double-count risk: only 6 of 634 distinct queued prompts also appear as user-record text, and cross-file copies (85) collapse via uuid dedup.
5. Subagent layout: agent-*.jsonl files live under <project>/<session-id>/subagents/ (session subdirectories), never at project top level; <project>/<session-id>/ session dirs are already skipped by discovery. The top-level agent- prefix filter remains defensive only.
6. Forked/branched copies preserve record uuids: 15 of 102 yielded uuids and 85 of 634 queued prompts appear in multiple files — dedup by uuid is correct as implemented.
7. history-sources.json: absent on this Mac — the archive registry is optional; missing roots handled as absent source.

Corrections implemented + synthetic fixtures added (tests/fixtures/sentiment/claude-code):
- Standalone queued_command attachment records are now extracted (new fixture lines; gold label 'queued attachment prompt, thanks' added to the da54f5 gold set).
- NEW false-positive class found and fixed: <local-command-stdout>/<local-command-stderr> echoes ride as user records (82 in corpus; they were 82 of the 117 records the old logic yielded). isInjectedText now filters them.
- User records with origin.kind present and != human (task-notification 1600, peer 278 in corpus) are now excluded.
- Test isolation fix: CLI unit tests now point claude/codex roots at nonexistent dirs instead of silently scanning the real Mac HOME (they passed on CI only because the VM had no real corpora).
- Unrelated meter bug fixed en route: computeMeter counted distinct dedupKeys as sessionsScanned (59 messages reported as 59 sessions on the real corpus); it now counts distinct sessionIds. Meter spec strengthened.

Real-corpus sanity after fixes: last 24h window = 59 human messages, 10 sessions, 5 fbomb tokens / 4 messages, 0 thanks (band 'cursing at the machine'), all claude-code; today = quiet. All 128 sentiment unit tests green; lint back to the single pre-existing benchmark error.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Closed: all seven format assumptions verified against the real Mac corpus; corrections (standalone queued_command attachment extraction, local-command-stdout/origin.kind filters) implemented with synthetic fixtures and a new gold label; CLI test isolation and the sessionsScanned meter bug fixed. 128 sentiment tests green. Evidence in the progress comment above.
